author: human
request:
Feature request: filter the vet list by specialty. Three product decisions
come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-9 is narrowed: free-text veterinarian search stays out of
  scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is in.
  Record the narrowing the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The JSON endpoint at /vets is reinstated as a supported surface — this
  filter is its first requested capability. Mint a fresh requirement for it;
  the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused.
- The filter is a URL contract only. Neither surface gains a form, dropdown,
  or other page control in this request; pagination links carry the
  parameter so filtered pages stay navigable. A visible control may come as
  a follow-up request.

Both vet list surfaces accept an optional `specialty` query parameter:

- /vets.html?specialty=<name> — the HTML page shows only vets holding that
  specialty; pagination applies to the filtered list.
- /vets?specialty=<name> — the JSON endpoint returns only those vets.

Matching is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive — not a prefix. A
specialty matching no vet yields the normal page or JSON document with an
empty vet list (HTTP 200). An empty or whitespace-only value behaves as if
the parameter were absent, like the empty owner search. Without the parameter
both endpoints behave as today. Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Existing vet feature package, no service layer (system-design § Package Structure, § Contracts). The filter repeats the owner-search shape: an optional request parameter on the controller, a Spring Data derived query on the repository, Page plus count for the HTML route. Adjustments recorded this dispatch: VetRepository gains specialty-narrowed reads, paged and whole, matched on the whole name ignoring case and selected distinct, with no @Cacheable. VetController binds an optional specialty on both routes and treats a blank value as absent, which is normalization (architecture-principles § Web controller row), not a business rule. The value is otherwise passed through untrimmed, per PRD edge case 5. The whole-name case-insensitive match lives in the query, not the controller. Contracts rows for Vet, Specialty, Vets, VetRepository, VetController and CacheConfiguration now carry REQ-VET-003 and/or REQ-VET-004. The Known Defects row 'machine-readable route serves no requirement' is removed because REQ-VET-004 now owns /vets. Scale and Load section added. Basis: grep and read of VetController/VetRepository/Vet/vetList.html (IDE oracle not connected; weaker basis).
integration_points: Binding, /vets.html and /vets: a request-scoped optional String request parameter 'specialty' (no default). No persisted type is bound. A null, empty or whitespace-only value selects the existing unfiltered read; any other value is passed to the repository exactly as given.

Repository boundary, matching semantics (whole name, letter case ignored, prefix 'rad' matches nothing, 'none' matches nothing, ' surgery ' matches nothing, every specialty of a matching vet still listed): a real VetRepository over the seeded H2 data in ClinicServiceTests (@DataJpaTest). The seed has radiology held by two vets and surgery by two, one of them also holding dentistry. testing-principles § Mocking Policy: a real implementation first.

Framework transport, VetControllerTests (@WebMvcTest + MockMvc, the sanctioned transport double): routing of the parameter to the filtered vs unfiltered read, blank-as-absent, HTTP 200 with empty list, JSON shape, paging-link carriage. The existing @MockitoBean VetRepository stub may be extended for these: it is a tolerated framework stub (testing-principles § Mocking Policy). A hand-written double would have to reimplement Spring Data's Page/derived-method surface, and the paging-link case needs more matching vets than the seed holds.

Template vetList.html: every paging link (numbered, first, previous, next, last) is built with Thymeleaf link-expression parameters, @{/vets.html(page=...,specialty=...)}, which URL-encode the value. Without a specialty the rendered links must be unchanged from today (no stray 'specialty' parameter); a null-valued parameter must be omitted, not rendered bare.
Machine-readable list stays unpaged (PRD edge case 2) and keeps the Vets wrapper.

patterns.description: optional search parameter, empty value treated as no filter, paged derived query with paging model attributes
existing findPaginated/addPaginationModel helpers to extend with the optional specialty; page size stays the local variable

risks.risk: Specialty-narrowed reads are keyed by request-supplied text; caching them in the 'vets' cache would let any caller grow a cache with no size limit (system-design § Scale and Load, Vet cache row; security-principles § Trust Boundaries, deny by default / least privilege).
risks.mitigation: No @Cacheable on the specialty-narrowed repository methods; only the unfiltered reads stay cached, as the Scale and Load Form column records.

risks.risk: Specialty names are not unique in any vendor schema, and the H2 vet_specialties table has no unique (vet, specialty) pair. A join on name can return one vet twice and inflate the page count (system-design § Scale and Load, specialty-narrowed row).
risks.mitigation: Distinct derived query (findDistinctBy...) so the paged count is distinct too.

risks.risk: The request-supplied name reaches the database (security-principles § Language Realization, injection into data access).
risks.mitigation: Spring Data derived query with IgnoreCase only; no concatenated JPQL or SQL. The IgnoreCase upper-cases both sides, so it is portable across H2, MySQL and PostgreSQL.

risks.risk: The request-supplied name is echoed into paging hrefs (security-principles, cross-site scripting through rendered data).
risks.mitigation: Thymeleaf link-expression parameters (URL-encoded, escaped); never the __${...}__ preprocessing string concatenation the current links use, for the specialty value.

risks.risk: Path scales with the vet set (system-design § Scale and Load, veterinarians and specialty-narrowed rows: unrecorded, treated as bounded).
risks.mitigation: Simplest readable form: one derived query, plus its count when paged.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Injection into data access: the request-supplied specialty reaches the database only as a bound argument of the Spring Data derived queries findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String) and findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String, Pageable) (VetRepository.java diff); grep -F for '@Query', 'createQuery', 'nativeQuery' under src/main/java/.../vet/ returned no matches, so no concatenated query text exists on this path.

Template injection removed, not added: the five paging links in vetList.html drop the '@{'/vets.html?page=__${i}__'}' preprocessing form for link-expression parameters such as '@{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})}', so the request-derived specialty is URL-encoded as a query parameter and never evaluated as a template expression; grep -F for '__$' and 'utext' in vetList.html returned no matches.

XSS: the specialty value is rendered only inside th:href link parameters, which Thymeleaf URL-encodes and attribute-escapes; it is not echoed as text anywhere in vetList.html (lines 1-26 read: only vet names and specialty.name from the database are rendered, via escaping th:text).

Cache safety: the new repository methods carry no @Cacheable, and their javadoc reads 'Not cached: the name is request-supplied', so arbitrary request values cannot grow the 'vets' cache without bound (cache-key exhaustion avoided); the existing cached findAll paths are unchanged.

Binding and surface: specialty is a scalar @RequestParam(required = false) String on two existing GET routes; no new endpoint, no new @ModelAttribute/@RequestBody target, no mutation, so the mass-assignment and surface-widening rows of docs/security-principles.md do not apply. Blank input normalizes to absent (asAbsentWhenBlank), and the result set on /vets is a subset of the pre-existing unfiltered list, so no new unbounded allocation.

Secrets: grep -i -E for password|secret|token|apikey|api_key|credential over added lines in the changeset matched only the system-design.md Security Context prose line 'Environment variables supplying the datasource credentials...', which names no value; no credential added.

Supply chain: build.gradle is not in the change set (git diff --stat -- build.gradle empty), no dependency change; dependencyCheckAnalyze is not configured (grep -F 'dependencyCheck' build.gradle no match), so no NVD match ran in this review; resolved runtimeClasspath shows spring-boot-thymeleaf 4.1.1, thymeleaf 3.1.5.RELEASE, tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind 3.1.5.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: The Done-when bullet says every paging link keeps the specialty, and the template changed five link kinds (numbered, first, previous, next, last in vetList.html). The test requests page 1 of 2 and asserts one substring, containsString("/vets.html?page=2&specialty=..."). The numbered link to page 2, the next link and the last link all render that same href, so the assertion passes if any one of them keeps the specialty. A regression that drops the specialty from next, last, first or previous leaves the test green. First and previous render only when currentPage > 1 (th:if="${currentPage > 1}" in vetList.html), and the test never requests page 2, so those two have no coverage at all.
findings.fix: Drive the paging-link assertions from a middle page of three: stub a PageImpl with PageRequest.of(1, PAGE_SIZE) and a total above two pages, request page=2 with the specialty, and assert each expected href (page=1, 3, and the first/previous/next/last targets) carries the encoded specialty. Count occurrences of the encoded specialty if per-link assertions are too verbose.

findings.description: Bare literals PageRequest.of(0, 1), isEqualTo(2) and hasSize(1) are Tier 3 mystery values under testing-principles.md § Three-Tier Data Naming. The 2 is the number of radiology vets in the seed and the 1 is the page size; neither is named, so the reader cannot tell that total=2 against page size=1 is what proves the count ignores paging.
findings.fix: Name them by role (FIRST_PAGE_INDEX, ONE_VET_PER_PAGE, RADIOLOGY_VET_COUNT) and derive the content size from the page size constant, as the file's other new constants do.
